limitations: Certification has logical same-process API integrity; Python privacy is not hostile same-interpreter isolation.
Reflective access to private module state, object.__setattr__, import hooks, or arbitrary code execution in the Kernel interpreter cannot be made cryptographically impossible by this design.
The certified origin must remain the same live in-memory object; generic serialization does not preserve certification authority.
The issuer-minted origin_id is a correlation identity, not a protected principle ID, signature, or independent authority.
Copied, deep-copied, replaced, mapping-rehydrated, JSON-rehydrated, or pickled origin results are distinct unissued objects and cannot certify.
Certificate pickle is rejected; certificate copy and deepcopy return the same immutable certificate.
Public result dataclass constructors remain available for compatibility, but manually constructed results have no private issuance attestation.
Only the approved P004, degree-peer, and parent-child fatal violation branches currently issue certifiable origins.
P023 remains nonfatal and cannot issue a certified structural invalidity.
Future reviewed structural validators require reviewed private producer registration before package bootstrap sealing.
No evidence-no-rescue behavior has been implemented.
No evidence evaluation, ranking, candidate generation, pattern interpretation, degree inference, orchestration, provider, TradingView, alert, network, or execution logic has been added.
The contract does not provide durable cross-process certification; that would require a separately reviewed protected-process or signing design.
STRUCTURAL-INVALIDITY-CONTRACT-V1 is a logical development baseline and is not physically protected.
